clue.text: The Church is after him, say, to deliver judgment

indicators.note: 'is after' places the church letters behind the other piece

parts.note: 'him' is an example of a part of speech that stands in for a noun
CE is the usual abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: The Church is pursuing some man, intending to pass sentence on him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is after' reads as the Church hunting someone down, but it is only a placement signal for the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to declare a verdict or ruling formally, as a judge does.

clue.text: Quietly fancy a witch-hunt

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
an urge is a desire or fancy

explanation.surface: A muted enthusiasm for persecuting supposed witches.
explanation.definitionFit: A purge is a campaign to root out and remove opponents, like a witch-hunt.

clue.text: Fruit supplier made love to cleaner in street

parts.note: O is love, nil in tennis scoring

indicators.note: 'in' says the cleaner's word goes inside the street's letters

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a street
a char is a British word for a cleaning lady

explanation.surface: An amorous encounter with a cleaner out on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' and 'to' are mere links; the surface's lovemaking is just tennis's nil.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot of fruit trees, so it supplies fruit.

clue.text: Circulate gold coin

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold
a bit is a small coin, as in a threepenny bit

explanation.surface: Put a gold coin into general use.
explanation.definitionFit: To orbit is to travel round and round something, to circle about it.

clue.text: Love to be on night shift

indicators.note: 'shift' says the letters of on night are moved into a new order

explanation.surface: Romance on a night-time work rota.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' looks like a work rota but rearranges ON NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis love means a score of zero, so love is a synonym for none at all.

clue.text: Complaint as regards public transport

parts.note: eyes, as a verb, means looks at or regards
a train is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A grumble concerning buses and trains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regards' looks part of 'as regards', meaning about, but it is EYES; 'as' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyestrain is tiredness or ache of the eyes, a medical complaint.

clue.text: It breaks and breaks around the West

indicators.note: 'around' says the rearranged letters wrap round the compass letter
the second 'breaks' says the word and is broken up and its letters rearranged

parts.note: W is the compass abbreviation for West

explanation.surface: Something that keeps breaking, shattering all around the western world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaks' turns AND into DAN, and 'around' puts W inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Day is said to break at first light, so daybreak is the thing that breaks.

clue.text: Title in fact much wished for

indicators.note: 'in' says the title's letters sit inside the other word

parts.note: a deed is a thing done, an accomplished fact
Sir is a title given to a knight

explanation.surface: A knighthood that is in fact greatly coveted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something desired is wanted or longed for, much wished for.

clue.text: Oppose having a base

parts.note: with means having, as in a man with a hat
a stand is a base that something rests on

explanation.surface: Object to owning a foundation.
explanation.definitionFit: To withstand is to resist or stand firm against something, to oppose it.

clue.text: Criticism for decent chap leading strike

indicators.note: 'leading' puts the chap's word in front of the other piece

parts.note: a brick is old British slang for a reliable, good-hearted person
to bat is to hit, as with a bat

explanation.surface: Disapproval aimed at a decent fellow for heading a walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strike' suggests industrial action but is just BAT, to hit; 'leading' puts BRICK first.
explanation.definitionFit: A brickbat, literally a thrown piece of brick, is figuratively a cutting remark or harsh criticism.

clue.text: German sub

parts.note: not a U-boat: the word for a substitute is borrowed from German

explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz is a German loanword meaning a replacement, usually an inferior substitute.

clue.text: Nit-picker takes notes in exercise books

indicators.note: 'in' says the notes sit inside the other letters

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
D and A are two musical notes

explanation.surface: A fussy teacher writes comments in pupils' exercise books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercise books' looks like one school item but splits into two abbreviations, with the notes put 'in' between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant is someone overly concerned with minor details and rules, a nit-picker.

clue.text: You won't care if you lose it

definitions.text: You won't care if you lose it

parts.words: You won't care if you lose it
parts.note: once you have lost this, you are no longer bothered about something

explanation.definitionFit: To lose interest is to stop caring, so the clue describes the thing whose loss means indifference.

clue.text: Noted and objected

definitions.meaning: to mind something is to heed or take note of it
to have ... something is to have objected to it

explanation.definitionFit: Mind means both to pay attention to and to dislike or object to, giving two past senses.

clue.text: Rude about vessel's prow being on the rocks

indicators.note: 'about' says the rude word goes around the single letter

parts.note: insolent means rudely disrespectful

indicators.note: a prow is the front of a ship, so the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A ship's bow breaking up on the rocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' sounds like a shipwreck but means bankrupt; 'about' puts V inside INSOLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm on the rocks is in financial ruin, unable to pay its debts.

clue.text: Orders hay to be put out for this animal

indicators.note: 'to be put out' says the letters of orders hay are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Someone requests fodder to be laid out for a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be put out' rearranges ORDERS HAY; the animal is one that would eat it.
explanation.definitionFit: This draught horse pulled a brewer's dray, a low cart, and would eat the hay.

clue.text: One with minor responsibilities in a newspaper

definitions.meaning: a person legally responsible for a child, a minor
a British daily paper of this name

explanation.definitionFit: A guardian looks after a minor; The Guardian is also a UK national newspaper.

clue.text: Prank ceased being funny when father came in

indicators.note: 'came in' says the father's letters enter the rearranged word
'being funny' says the letters of ceased are behaving oddly, rearranged

parts.note: PA is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A practical joke stopped being amusing once Dad turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being funny' rearranges the letters into ESCADE, and 'came in' puts Dad inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapade is a daring or mischievous adventure, much like a prank.

clue.text: A pamphlet said to make a personal appeal

indicators.note: 'said' says the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: A leaflet supposedly making an appeal to the reader personally.
explanation.walkthrough: A TRACT spoken sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To attract is to draw someone by personal charm or appeal.

clue.text: Guaranteed safe, when in extremity

indicators.note: 'in' says the safe word sits inside the extremity's letters

parts.note: an end is an extremity
sure means safe or reliable, as in a sure bet

explanation.surface: Made certain of safety when in dire straits.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensured means made certain, so it is a synonym of guaranteed.

clue.text: Not a person of substance, presumably

definitions.text: Not a person of substance, presumably

parts.words: Not a person of substance, presumably
parts.note: read literally, someone with no physical body would have no substance

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on someone of no importance.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobody is an unimportant person, and taken literally someone with no body lacks substance.

clue.text: Young Italian graduate doctor in love

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
O is love, nil in tennis

explanation.surface: A young Italian graduate doctor who has fallen in love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is kept as its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bambino is Italian for a baby or young child.

clue.text: Seizes egg collections

definitions.meaning: sets of eggs laid at one time in a nest

explanation.definitionFit: To clutch is to grip hard, and a clutch is also a batch of eggs laid together.

clue.text: Private doctor comes in this month

indicators.note: 'comes in' says the doctor's letters go inside the month's

parts.note: INST, short for instant, is old business shorthand for the current month
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: A personal physician arrives during the current month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' suggests a private doctor, but it is the definition, meaning innermost.
explanation.definitionFit: Inmost means deepest or most secret, so one's inmost thoughts are private ones.

clue.text: Experience part of the main current

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Feel a small portion of the ocean's flow.
explanation.definitionFit: To incur something, such as costs or anger, is to undergo or experience it.

clue.text: Grim end to a ship

definitions.meaning: the rear part of a vessel

explanation.definitionFit: Stern means severe in manner, and the stern is also the back end of a ship.

clue.text: Go back by air?

indicators.note: 'back' says the word for by is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wondering whether to make the return journey by plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go back' reads as one phrase about returning, but 'Go' alone is the definition; 'back' turns PER round.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair to a place is a formal way of saying to go there.

clue.text: Criminal who runs a 13 down business

definitions.meaning: an official appointed to manage a bankrupt company

explanation.definitionFit: A receiver is both a fence for stolen goods and the official administering a failed firm's affairs.

clue.text: Indication that a writer's revision is not better

definitions.text: Indication that a writer's revision is not better

parts.words: Indication that a writer's revision is not better
parts.note: a proofreading mark telling the printer to ignore a correction and keep the original

explanation.surface: A sign that an author's rewrite was no improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet, Latin for let it stand, is the mark restoring text that was altered or deleted.

clue.text: I wondered about getting a bedcover

indicators.note: 'about' says the letters of the two words are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone muses on whether to buy a quilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' shuffles the nine letters of I WONDERED.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt filled with soft down, laid on a bed as a cover.
